title: Rosatom Chief Defends Paks II Timeline at IAEA Conference as Magyar Government Reviews Deal
detail: On the sidelines of the IAEA General Conference in Vienna around September 14–15, Rosatom Director General Alexey Likhachev said 2026 construction milestones on the Paks II nuclear expansion remained on schedule — Unit 5's foundation slab (started February) nearly complete, Unit 6 preparatory work commencing, and French-made turbine components already in production — and that the plant's design accounts for the low-Danube-water conditions seen during summer 2026's drought. Likhachev said Rosatom stood ready for dialogue with Budapest 'at any format, including government leadership level' and awaited concrete proposals. The remarks come as PM Péter Magyar's government runs a comprehensive due-diligence review of the €12.5B project awarded without tender to Rosatom in 2014; Magyar has warned total costs could double and flagged major delays, noting roughly 1 trillion forints (€2.7B) spent to date with only excavation work substantially complete. The modified 2026 budget allocates 206.6 billion forints (€563M) to the project this year.

media.caption: Rosatom's Alexey Likhachev defends the Paks II timeline as Hungary's government reviews the deal

title: Momentum's Fekete-Győr Files Criminal Complaint Against Orbán Over NVVH Threats
detail: Momentum politician András Fekete-Győr filed a criminal complaint against Viktor Orbán at Budapest Police Headquarters on September 15, alleging preparation for violence against a public official and incitement. The complaint targets Orbán's September 13 Bayer Show remarks that Fidesz would 'track down' and publicize the names of every NVVH anti-corruption office employee if the party returns to power, comparing the agency to the communist-era ÁVH secret police. NVVH President Anna Unger said 'no one has the right to threaten or intimidate our staff members,' while PM Péter Magyar argued in parliament that Orbán's remarks could constitute the criminal offense of violence against a public official, which carries a possible prison sentence under Hungarian law.

media.caption: András Fekete-Győr files a criminal complaint against Viktor Orbán over threats to NVVH staff
